Definition: from G1722 and βριμάομαι (to snort with anger); to have indignation on, i.e. (transitively) to blame, (intransitively) to sigh with chagrin, (specially) to sternly enjoin:--straitly charge, groan, murmur against.
BiblicalUsage: embrimáomai is how Scripture says to be deeply moved, to sternly charge. In Matthew 9:30, the text says "and Jesus straitly charged them." In Mark 1:43, the text says "And he straitly charged him."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that embrimáomai matters because compassion is not pity from a distance; it is drawing near and doing something. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Raising of Lazarus; Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy; The Anointing at Bethany
